notas.titulo: The beginning: homogeneity, gravity and entropy
notas.texto: let's go to a brief explanation directed afterwards to quantum mechanics In the beginning, matter was distributed homogeneously — the same density at every point, varying only 1 part in 100 thousand — and isotropic, with no privileged direction. But it was not constant: the temperature was falling, because the universe was expanding. And here is the point that inverts intuition: uniform is the most probable state for a gas in a box, and the least probable for matter with gravity. Gravity is attractive, so it gains entropy by clumping — clumping releases potential energy that turns into heat, and the heat opens up many more microstates than matter loses by becoming localized. The state of maximum entropy of a mass in a region is a black hole: for one solar mass, 10 ⁷⁷ against 10 ⁵⁸ for the current Sun. So the universe was born in the most improbable gravitational configuration there is. And no matter was created after that. The baryons were fixed in the first second; all the rest was assembly — nuclei at 3 minutes, atoms at 380 thousand years, stars afterwards. The same matter, different arrangements. Clumping did not start earlier because it could not : the photons were coupled to matter, and radiation pressure beat gravity. At 380 thousand years the atoms formed, the photons decoupled, the pressure got out of the way — and gravity started to win. The irregularities of 1 in 100 thousand started to grow. That is when entropy rises. Not because entropy does something: it is the accounting of the clumping, not the cause. Each star that forms is gravitational order being spent. And the end is the equality of everything through the exhaustion of that order. Beginning and end have the same uniform temperature. The difference is that at the beginning there was everything to do.

notas.titulo: Ax1 — Every fragment is inside the Whole
notas.texto: Every fragment is inside the Whole. Nothing is left out. ⊆ and not ∈ because A is prior and is cut out — it is not assembled from the fragments.

notas.titulo: Ax2 — No fragment is the Whole
notas.texto: No fragment is the Whole. It is the axiom that makes it impossible for any part to take the place of the whole.

notas.titulo: Ax3 — There are at least two distinct fragments
notas.texto: There are at least two distinct fragments. Why both clauses: i ≠ j does not guarantee fᵢ ≠ fⱼ — two names can point to the same object. A difference of label is not a difference of thing.

notas.titulo: Ax4 — The Whole is not one of its own items
notas.texto: The Whole is not one of its own items. It blocks infinite regress and the neighborhood of Russell. In ZF this is a theorem (Regularity) — if you declare ZF, it comes off the list. [D/F]

notas.titulo: Ax5 — Written in the text as ⋃ᵢ∈I fᵢ = A: the fragments cover the Whole
notas.texto: Written in the text as ⋃ᵢ∈I fᵢ = A: the fragments cover the Whole. Nothing of A is left uncovered. (Here written element by element: x is in A exactly when it is in some fragment.)

notas.titulo: Ax6 — Written in the text as ⋂ᵢ∈I fᵢ ≠ ∅: there is something common to ALL
notas.texto: Written in the text as ⋂ᵢ∈I fᵢ ≠ ∅: there is something common to ALL. It is what keeps K from being empty. ⚠ It has to be the total intersection, not pairwise. Three sets can intersect in pairs without any point common to all three.

notas.titulo: Ax7 — No fragment belongs to another fragment
notas.texto: No fragment belongs to another fragment. It does not follow from the other six. Aristotle, Politics 1255b: "the slave is a part of the master" = f_slave ∈ f_master. Ax7 forbids exactly that.

notas.titulo: Definition — K, the Essence
notas.texto: K = ⋂ᵢ fᵢ: what is common to all the fragments. Example from the text: f₁ = {a,b,c}, f₂ = {b,c,d} → K = {b,c}, A = {a,b,c,d}. The principle of the axioms was built with Spinoza's premise about Essence.

Construction of the nerve (Čech): a vertex per fragment · an edge when two touch · a triangle when three touch · and so on. Nerve Theorem: if the cover is good (contractible intersections), the nerve has the shape of the whole — the shape of the whole is encoded in who touches whom. This makes T3 livable: you do not reach A, but you compute its shape from the pattern of the encounters.

Formulas (FORMALIZATION PROPOSED by the app, review it — finite version): every pair and every triple of fragments touch. It follows from Ax6 (K not empty): the nerve is a full simplex, and by the Nerve Theorem the shape of the Whole is that of a point. The topological part (good cover, contractible intersections) stays only in the text.

Checked by the app (2026-10-12): both follow from Ax6 (all worlds up to 5 objects); without Ax6, they do not follow.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T12 — Absorption Theorem
notas.texto:
Hypotheses: H1 D2 and D3; H2 motion on a straight line; H3 A (m_A, v_A) and B (m_B, v_B); H4 B ahead of A and v_B < v_A (there is contact). r = m_B/m_A.
(a) e = 0: v_B′ = (v_A + r v_B)/(1 + r).
(b) r → 0 ⟹ v_B′ → v_A.
(c) Δv_B = (v_A − v_B)/(1 + r) grows when v_B decreases; v_B′ decreases when v_B decreases.
(d) E_def = ½ μ (v_A − v_B)² (1 − e²), μ = m_A m_B/(m_A + m_B).
(e) any e: v_B′ = (v_A + r v_B)/(1 + r) + e (v_A − v_B)/(1 + r). With e = 1 and r → 0: v_B′ → 2v_A − v_B.
Proof: conservation of momentum (D3) and restitution v_B′ − v_A′ = e (v_A − v_B). ∎
Corollaries C1 weighted average · C2 adoption · C3 trade-off · C4 launch or absorption · C5 no contact, no theorem.
Example 1 (a 100 t train at 10 m/s, a 10 t car, e ≈ 0): car at +5 → 9.55 m/s (changes 4.55; the train loses 0.45; 114 kJ) · stopped → 9.09 (9.09; 0.91; 455 kJ) · at −2 → 8.91 (10.91; 1.09; 655 kJ). Example 2: a ball at −10 m/s against a truck at +20 m/s, e ≈ 1 → 50 m/s. Example 3: gravity assist (Voyager).
Social examples [M]: S1 the apprentice · S2 the one who goes to argue · S3 the one who arrives dismantling what they thought · S4 the one who admires from afar. Limit: between people, H4 depends on a decision by the other, which no axiom represents.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T13 — Coalescence: total absorption traps
notas.texto:
Joins T12 + T8. (a) With e = 0 and no external force, the two stay together forever. (b) The response to an impulse J falls from J/m_B to Δv = J/(m_A + m_B) = (J/m_B)·r/(1 + r). (c) If r is small, you come to see only what they see; by T8, you do not gather D independent bases. ∎
The way out: to separate, e > 0 is needed; absorbing everything and staying free is impossible in the same encounter. Valuing both equally [D], e(1 − e²) is maximum at e = 1/√3 ≈ 0.58.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T14 — Diffusion: random exposure stalls displacement
notas.texto:
Joins T6 + T7 + kinetic theory. In a medium without a gradient, with encounters in random directions: (a) the displacement grows like √t; (b) the larger σ, the smaller 𝒟; (c) with a directed force F, the collisions work as friction: v_drift = Fλ/(m v̄) ∝ 1/(nσ).
Proof: N random steps of size λ, with N = v̄t/λ, give a mean square displacement Nλ²; between collisions the force accelerates for τ = λ/v̄. ∎ [F] (Drude, 1900). Social [M]: the crowded beach acts as friction.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T15 — Dominance of acceleration
notas.texto:
For any initial advantages Δx₀ and Δv₀, if Δa ≠ 0, then for large t Δx(t) = Δx₀ + Δv₀ t + ½ Δa t² is dominated by the term in t². ∎ T5 is the case Δx₀ = 0. Social [M]: in the long run, the rate of improvement beats the current level.

Check: ✓ checked by hand (algebra and numerical examples match).

Formula: for large t, |Δx₀ + Δv₀t| stays below |½Δa t²|.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T16 — Hierarchy of regimes
notas.texto:
Random encounters ∝ √t; constant velocity ∝ t; constant acceleration ∝ t². The one above is always overtaken by the one below: √t/t → 0 and t/t² → 0. ∎
Example (𝒟 = 1, v = 0.1, a = 0.002): t = 1 → 1.4 / 0.1 / 0.001 · t = 100 → 14 / 10 / 10 · t = 10,000 → 141 / 1,000 / 100,000. Short-term noise looks like progress.

Check: ✓ checked by hand (algebra and numerical examples match). (table checked: √(2t), 0.1t and ½·0.002·t².)

Formulas: √(2t) < t for t > 2; t < ½at² for t > 2/a; and numbers from the table (t = 10,000).

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T17 — Mass: the only variable that nothing rewrites
notas.texto:
In the state z = (x, v, m, σ): x changes through interaction (via v); v changes through interaction (Δv = J/m); σ changes through choice; m changes neither through interaction nor through choice — and it is m that decides how much interactions rewrite v (T2) and turn the direction (T3.2).
Proof from the text: D1 defines m as constant. D2 alters only p, hence only v. No axiom has dm/dt. ∎
The hole: a law dm/dt = g(…) is missing.

Check: ⚠ D1, as written, only says mᵢ > 0 — it does not say that m is constant. And if m varied, D2 (dp/dt = ΣF) would also change v because of dm/dt. For the proof to hold, D1 needs to say "dmᵢ/dt = 0" (or "mᵢ constant"); T4 also depends on this.

Formula: the mass does not change in the encounter — Z3 should say that it does NOT follow from D1–D8 (it is the hole that T17 itself points out).

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T18 — Escalation
notas.texto:
Hypotheses: H0 the stimulus gives reward from the beginning; H1 D8; H2 the person seeks to keep the same response r*. To get r* at exposure k: s_k = r*/h(k), increasing.
Proof: s_k · h(k) = r*; h decreasing ⟹ 1/h increasing. ∎ It holds for any habituation, not only the exponential.
Example (β = 0.2, r* = 1): k = 0 → 1.0 · 5 → 2.7 · 10 → 7.4 · 20 → 54.6. Corollary: with s_max = 10, impossible to keep after exposure 11; ways out: accept less, stop or switch stimulus (search for novelty). [F] in pharmacology (tolerance).

Check: ✓ checked by hand (algebra and numerical examples match). (e^(0.2k): 1; 2.72; 7.39; 54.6; limit 10 → k ≤ 11.5.)

Formula: s_k = r*/h(k) grows with k.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T19 — Collapse of the alarm
notas.texto:
The moral alarm also habituates: A(s, Hₐ) = s · hₐ(Hₐ). Advancing in small steps δ, the alarm at each step is ΔA ≈ δ · hₐ(Hₐ): small and smaller each time. Each new step is compared with the previous one, not with zero. ∎ With T18: the intensity sought rises, the alarm felt falls; no isolated step looks big. Milgram's scale, 15 volts at a time. [F] mechanism; [M] applied to values.

Check: ✓ consistent with D8 (qualitative argument).

Formulas: the alarm of a step δ = d is d·h(H): it falls with each repetition and never exceeds the step itself — it follows from D8. Checked by the app (2026-10-12): both follow from D8 (Z3, for any size).

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T20 — From pleasure to lack
notas.texto:
When the stimulus ends, the state falls below normal, and this fall grows with the repetitions. Basis: Solomon and Corbit (1974), opponent process; Koob and Le Moal (2001). At the beginning one repeats for the reward; later, to flee the lack. [F] in chemical dependence; [M] for other habits.

Check: it does not follow from D8 (it is a new empirical law cited from the literature); it stands as a hypothesis supported by studies.

Formulas: lack(H) = how much the state falls below normal when the stimulus ends, after H repetitions: zero at the beginning and increasing. As the check says, it does not follow from D8 — the engine should answer that it does not follow (it is a new empirical law). Checked by the app (2026-10-12): Z3 does not prove it from D1–D8, as the check said.

notas.titulo: Dynamics · T21 — Symmetry: the same mechanism builds virtue
notas.texto:
D8 does not know whether the act is good or bad: the cost of any repeated act also falls with repetition. Habit consolidates whatever is repeated (Aristotle, Nicomachean Ethics II.1). Reversal: spontaneous recovery and dishabituation. Limit (H0): T18 only holds if the act gives reward from the first time; for almost everyone, causing suffering is aversive — habit lowers the brake without creating the desire.

Check: ✓ consistent with D8 and with the limit H0 of T18.

Formulas: the cost c·h(H) of any repeated act falls, whether the act is good or bad (the formula has no place for that); and the limit H0: if the act gives no reward (r ≤ 0), the intensity sought r/h does not grow — it needs h > 0 (D8′), like T18. Checked by the app (2026-10-12): the first follows from D8; the second follows with D8′ turned on (without it, Z3 does not prove it).

The list of "who exists"; i, j are elements of I — a part, a person.
fᵢ = f(i): the fragment i, a part of the whole (an object inside the Whole).
K = ⋂ᵢ fᵢ: what is common to all the fragments.

Concebido(x, y): x is conceived through y.
